overview: After 1.e4 h6 2.d4 Black strikes with 2...e5, offering the e5 pawn. White can take with 3.dxe5 and hold the extra pawn, with Black hoping for development and the open d-file. It is a rare, speculative gambit built on a very odd 1...h6.

white_ideas.idea: Take on e5 and defend the extra pawn with Nf3 or Bd3
Develop normally and trade queens if Black plays ...Qe7 ideas
Use the central space and the tempo lost on h6

black_ideas.idea: Recapture or harass e5 with ...Nc6, ...Qe7 and ...Bc5
Open the d-file and develop quickly
Take advantage of White's misplaced pieces for a quick attack

typical_structures.structure: Open centre with White a pawn up on e5

character.notes: Black offers a pawn on move two after a wasted move, so forcing and risky.

gambit.notes: After 3.dxe5 White is a pawn up and the pawn is not clearly regained.

soundness.notes: Black has used a tempo on h6 and a pawn for little, so it is dubious.

structure.notes: The d- and e-pawns come off, leaving open lines.

approach.notes: Almost never chosen by strong players.

level.notes: Few lines to learn, but it is not sound enough to be a good repertoire choice.

character.reason: A pawn is offered at move two, so play is risky for the side that goes wrong.

gambit.reason: Black offers the e5 pawn that White can take with 3.dxe5.

soundness.reason: Black spends a tempo on h6 and loses a pawn with little to show for it.

structure.reason: The central pawns trade or fall, leaving open lines.

approach.reason: Strong players hardly ever play the Carr Defence or this gambit.

level.reason: It is dubious, so not Beginner, and not complex enough to be Advanced.

plans.reason: Black hopes development makes up for the pawn.
